neighbours.label: the word right before a noun naming a sphere or way of life that someone enters, leaves or endures (civilian/public/married → 'life', teaching → 'profession'); the same verbs with a concrete object stay quiet
fire: After the war many soldiers struggled to adjust to civilian life.
The senator announced that she would retire from public life next year.
He never quite got used to married life.
She missed the city but slowly settled into village life.
Burned out after a decade, he decided to leave the nursing profession.
Released after nine years, he found it hard to cope with ordinary life outside.
The young monk soon grew weary of monastic life.
Her parents warned her about the hardships of the acting profession.
quiet: After the war many soldiers struggled to rebuild the bridge.
The senator announced that she would visit the factory next year.
He never quite got used to the new keyboard.
She missed the city but slowly painted the kitchen.
Burned out after a decade, he decided to sell the house.
Released after nine years, he found it hard to open the heavy door.
The young monk soon finished copying the long manuscript.
Her parents warned her about the ice on the steps.
